title: GitHub MCP Part 2: The First Driver
text: Hi, I'm Rishika. This is part two of three. Last time I built six readonly tools for GitHub MCP assistant, the toolbox. Nobody was using them yet. This video is the first driver, a manual client. A human me for now picks a tool from a menu and runs it directly. No AI involved. That comes in part three. The manual client is the simplest possible way to use the toolbox. A numbered menu.

title: How the Manual Client Works: The Numbered Menu
text: It lists the six abilities. A human reads them, types a number to pick one, and passes in whatever that tool needs. It calls that one tool and shows you exactly what comes back. The raw result, nothing polished, nothing interpreted. Here's the loop. The menu prints. The human picks a tool. The client asks for whatever that tool needs, a repository name, maybe a file path or a keyword,

title: Request and Response: Passing Arguments Straight Through
text: And passes those arguments straight through. It calls that one tool and prints the raw output exactly as the tool returned it. Then it goes right back to the menu. Why build this before anything smarter? Because it forces you to understand exactly what each tool asks for and exactly what it hands back, the request and the response before an AI ever touches it. title: Why Build a Manual Client First?
text: Retire once an AI agent exists. This becomes the debugging harness you keep reusing for the rest of the project. Anytime you need to check one tool directly, where this honestly falls short, it only works if you already know exactly which tool you need and exactly what to type. title: The Lifelong Debugging Harness
text: It has no idea what that means. It can't combine tools and it can't read between the lines of what you're actually asking. That gap is exactly what an AI agent is for. Where things stand, part two done. The same six tools from part one now actually usable through a numbered menu a human drives directly.

title: Honest Limits: Rigid Inputs vs. Plain English
text: Building it forced a clear look at exactly what each tool asks for and hands back. And it's not just a stepping stone. It's the debugging harness this project keeps reusing. What's still missing? Anything that understands a real question in plain English. That's the AI agent in part three.
